Well, almost all ideas are "viral" in that you can spread them by communicating them to others, so the meme (the idea that explaining jokes is annoying) does counter the first by preventing the spread/belief in it. There's nothing anomalous about anything in this SCP or the counter-meme, but that's perfectly fine because a "meme" isn't actually inherently anomalous, despite what many on the site believe.

I propose a counter-meme: the idea that misunderstanding what a "meme" is is really annoying

item.content:encoded:
Given that this SCP is "Explained," I think it would benefit from making a joke of being obvious and over-explaining its own joke at the end. Something like,

"Although this phenomenon was initially believed to be anomalous in nature, further research has determined that some people are actually terrible at telling jokes for utterly mundane reasons. Please disregard the preceding article. The poorly told jokes were not a result of anything supernatural; it can all be attributed to joke tellers who lacked confidence in either their own joke-telling ability or their audience's ability to discern the humor in the joke. This lack of confidence led the joke-tellers to over-explain their own jokes, thus making the jokes less funny. Jokes are always less funny when you have to explain them. I hope this clears everything up."
